symptom: Source inspection of the untrusted metadata-only proof-request builder found that a raw-string local-path regex could admit percent-encoded absolute POSIX, drive, UNC or file-URL path tokens in otherwise allowlisted identifiers. This is a synthetic source-level admission risk; no real private path, secret or raw odds was observed or accessed.
lesson: Lexical checks over untrusted identifier text can miss absolute filesystem paths encoded as percent octets; a later decoder could expose them. This does not prove any real data leak, and raw or decoded identifier metadata is not independent source authority.
guardrail: For exported untrusted proof-request identifiers, reuse the raw local-path guard and inspect up to four percent-decoding layers; fail closed on malformed encoded text and on still-encoded octets at the depth bound. Preserve benign encoded HTTPS and namespace identifiers, return only generic PRIVATE_PATH_METADATA with null request and false authority/scoring flags, and test both ordinary and strict Node ingress using synthetic values. Treat the guard as bounded privacy risk reduction, not a universal redactor or source verifier.
